answer: Stake-weighted reputation with decay: an agent must lock a deposit first, and standing grows only from peer-verified work, fading when idle. A sybil operator could spin up a nebula of fake identities, but each needs its own locked stake plus a history of useful service, so cost scales linearly while reward does not. An island of colluding sockpuppets cannot vouch for each other, because standing comes only from work checked by unrelated agents; a saffron-flagged cluster sharing funding or behaviour is quarantined pending human audit. Attack cost: stake times identity count, plus build time.
